item.title: ScreenConnect MSP Breaches, eMudhra CA Revocations, and Notion AI Transcript Exposure
item.content:encoded:
Window: 11 Nov 19:00 → 11 Nov 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

Active ScreenConnect attacks breach MSPs, impact dozens of organizations — Must Read

Attackers are compromising MSP ScreenConnect environments to push rogue remote-access clients to customer devices, affecting at least six MSPs and 286 endpoints across 47 organizations. ConnectWise and Huntress urge partners to avoid interactive sessions with suspected compromised devices, review Run Command history, revoke sessions, reset credentials, and check for listed indicators of compromise.

  • Huntress identified an active campaign in which compromised cloud-hosted ScreenConnect environments at managed service providers were used to deploy rogue ScreenConnect clients to customer devices.
  • As of Huntress’s report, the campaign had affected six managed service providers and at least 286 endpoints across 47 organizations, with the number continuing to rise.
  • The attackers used ScreenConnect’s Run Command feature to install remote-access clients outside the legitimate managed service provider’s ScreenConnect environment.
  • ConnectWise said it was investigating the malicious activity and advised partners to avoid interactive sessions with suspected compromised devices, review account activity, revoke active sessions, reset credentials from a trusted device, and verify multifactor authentication.
  • Huntress said its telemetry pointed to compromised credentials and hijacked support sessions, but it had not determined how the attackers initially accessed the affected managed service provider environments.

Technologies: remote-access, antivirus

Products: screenconnect, microsoft-defender

Vendors: connectwise, huntress, microsoft, virustotal

eMudhra revokes 8 more CA certificates after private key mishap — Should Read

eMudhra revoked eight additional intermediate CA certificates after a faulty key-transfer script exposed RSA private-key material in host memory, bringing the total affected intermediates to 16. The incident prompted major vendors to block the compromised trust chains, and eMudhra plans to exit the publicly trusted TLS certificate business.

  • eMudhra revoked eight additional RSA intermediate certificate authority certificates after finding that a custom Python key-transfer script processed private-key material in the host computer's memory rather than solely inside secure hardware.
  • The additional revocations bring the total number of affected eMudhra intermediate certificates to 16, including eight ECDSA certificates whose private keys were reduced to one byte and could be recovered by testing 256 values.
  • The flawed script was used in April 2025 to transfer certificate authority keys between hardware security module vendors after delays obtaining new hardware.
  • Mozilla, Google, Apple, and Microsoft released protections to block trust in the compromised eMudhra certificate chains.
  • eMudhra plans to leave the publicly trusted TLS certificate business, stop issuing under its remaining G1 hierarchy by November 16, and has commissioned a KPMG review expected by December 4.

Technologies: operating-system, browser

Products: windows

Vendors: emudhra, mozilla, google, apple, microsoft

Notion says Fireworks breach exposed customer AI chat transcripts — Should Read

Notion says a breach at AI vendor Fireworks AI exposed Notion AI chat transcripts from its Insights dataset for less than 1% of users. Affected users should review incident notices and rotate any passwords, API keys, or credentials entered in those chats.

  • Notion disclosed that a security breach at its AI infrastructure provider, Fireworks AI, exposed Notion AI chat transcripts from a small number of workspaces.
  • The exposed transcripts came from the dataset used for Notion’s Insights feature, which lets workspace administrators view how their teams use AI and has now been disabled.
  • Notion stopped sending traffic to Fireworks AI, deleted its data from the vendor’s systems, and halted training runs by November 3 after being alerted to an exposed dataset.
  • Notion says fewer than 1% of its users are affected, and most of the affected transcripts were not labeled with the author or the workspace they came from.
  • Notion advises affected users to rotate passwords, API keys, and other credentials that they entered into affected chats.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: notion-ai, insights, fireworks-ai

Vendors: notion, fireworks-ai

Log Analysis Field Guide: Tips for Spotting Patterns and Red Flags — Optional

This guide explains how to analyze logs by focusing on timestamps, repetition, normal behavior baselines, and targeted filtering to identify suspicious activity. Key red flags include repeated failed logins followed by success, after-hours access, impossible travel, unexpected account changes, and unusual processes or network connections.

  • Logs record digital activity such as logins, file downloads, and network connections, helping answer who performed an action, what happened, when it happened, and where it originated.
  • Core log elements commonly include a timestamp, source system, event type, user or process, and whether the activity succeeded or failed.
  • Analysts should look for repetition, suspicious timing, and behavior that differs from normal activity, while using filters to focus on relevant entries.
  • Red flags include repeated failed logins followed by a successful login, unexpected after-hours activity, impossible travel indicators, modified accounts, and unusual processes or connections.
  • The article recommends documenting searches, checking whether activity has occurred before, comparing it with known bad behavior, and deciding whether escalation is needed.

Products: security-datasets, evtx-attack-samples, mitre-attack

Vendors: otrf, mitre

item.title: AntiFox-Linked AWS Secret Theft and Critical Zoom Workplace Flaws
item.content:encoded:
Window: 11 Nov 15:00 → 11 Nov 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

Critical Zoom Workplace Flaw Could Allow Unauthenticated Remote Privilege Escalation — Must Read

Zoom patched two critical Zoom Workplace for Windows flaws, CVE-2026-108186 and CVE-2026-108187, that could let unauthenticated remote attackers escalate privileges. Organizations should update to version 7.1.8 or later to remediate the affected versions.

  • Zoom released updates for Zoom Workplace for Windows to address two security flaws that could enable privilege escalation.
  • CVE-2026-108186 is an improper input validation flaw with a CVSS score of 9.6 that affects Zoom Workplace for Windows versions 7.1.0 through before 7.1.8.
  • CVE-2026-108187 is an origin validation flaw with a CVSS score of 8.1 that affects Zoom Workplace for Windows versions before 7.1.5.
  • According to the article, either flaw could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to escalate privileges without special permissions or access.
  • Zoom did not state that these vulnerabilities are being exploited in the wild, but users are advised to apply the latest patches.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: zoom-workplace, windows

Vendors: zoom, microsoft

The XG Files: Falcon C2 Flying Under The (Browser) Radar — Should Read

Unit 42 uncovered Falcon (XG), a browser-based espionage framework used against government targets in the Middle East and Southeast Asia to steal credentials, emails, cookies and communications through injected JavaScript and malicious Chrome/Firefox extensions. Falcon can also deploy the Rust-based Antino implant, which uses Microsoft OneDrive for command and control and persistence.

  • Unit 42 identified Falcon, also called XG or Xiàng Gē, as a command-and-control framework that uses malicious JavaScript in compromised websites to control and collect data from victims’ browsers.
  • Falcon was observed targeting government entities in one Middle Eastern country and four Southeast Asian countries between March and May 2026, including foreign affairs, defense, interior, law-enforcement and justice organizations.
  • Falcon can sideload Chrome and Firefox extensions disguised as a PDF viewer, giving operators access to browser credentials, cookies, web traffic, clipboard activity, browsing history, downloads and selected messaging services.
  • Falcon maintains encrypted WebSocket communications and can use a victim’s browser as a proxy to access resources with that victim’s saved credentials and active login sessions.
  • Falcon also delivered Antino, a Rust-based Windows implant that uses Microsoft OneDrive to receive commands, upload data and establish persistence through the Windows Registry Run key.

Technologies: browser, cloud-platform, object-storage, operating-system

Products: falcon-c2, antino, microsoft-onedrive, windows, google-chrome, mozilla-firefox, roundcube

Vendors: microsoft, google, mozilla, roundcube-project

Iran-backed network directed London attacks over FaceTime, US prosecutors say — Should Read

U.S. prosecutors allege that an IRGC-linked Kataib Hezbollah network remotely directed and recorded arson, stabbing, and attempted attacks on Jewish, American, and military-linked sites across Europe, including London, using FaceTime and other apps. Evidence recovered from a defendant’s seized iPhone reportedly documented the coordination, propaganda recordings, and plots including an attempted attack on RAF Fairford.

  • A U.S. superseding indictment alleges that three men linked to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and Kataib Hezbollah orchestrated attacks and attempted attacks at Jewish, American, and military-linked sites across Europe.
  • Prosecutors say attackers in London received live instructions over FaceTime during arson incidents targeting a Jewish charity building, Iran International, and a synagogue, while the calls were recorded for propaganda.
  • The indictment alleges that the network later planned an attack on RAF Fairford using vans, fuel, potential shrapnel, and intended explosives, but British authorities reported finding petrol and no explosives after stopping the vehicles.
  • Much of the cited evidence was recovered from Mohammad al-Saadi’s iPhone, including recorded FaceTime calls, raw attack footage, and messages with a Kataib Hezbollah contact.
  • Mohsen Mohajeri and Mohammed Ali al-Hassani are at large and believed to be in Iran, while al-Saadi has been jailed in New York since May.

Products: facetime, icloud

Vendors: apple

Maersk confirms data breach as WhiteArmor ransomware demands $5 million — Should Read

Maersk confirmed a breach of an isolated legacy LF Logistics system, while the WhiteArmor ransomware group claims it stole about 100GB of data and is demanding $5 million. Maersk says there is no evidence that sensitive data or other company and customer systems were affected.

  • Maersk confirmed that a threat actor breached systems belonging to a company it previously acquired and stole data.
  • WhiteArmor listed Maersk on its leak site, demanded $5 million in Bitcoin, and claimed to have stolen about 100GB of data from the OCF/LF Logistics platform.
  • Maersk said the incident is isolated to a local system, with no indication of impact on other Maersk systems or customer and partner integrations.
  • WhiteArmor claimed the stolen data includes nearly 30,000 driver records, plaintext passwords, privileged administrator accounts, delivery receipts, inventory records, and mobile-device logs.
  • Maersk said its investigation is ongoing and that current evidence indicates no sensitive data has been disclosed.

Products: ocf-lf-logistics-platform

Vendors: maersk, lf-logistics

Hackers use AntiFox AI agents in AWS credential-theft attacks — Should Read

Attackers are hosting the AntiFox open-source AI penetration-testing platform on Alibaba Cloud to automate intrusions against web servers and AWS environments, including webshell deployment and theft of production secrets. Defenders should investigate unusual IIS activity alongside bursts of denied and successful AWS API calls, then revoke exposed credentials and sessions.

  • Arctic Wolf observed Alibaba Cloud systems hosting self-managed AntiFox instances linked to malicious activity against internet-facing web services and associated AWS environments.
  • In one reported intrusion, an attacker deployed an ASPX webshell on an exposed IIS server, executed operating-system commands, and copied configuration and log files into a web-accessible directory.
  • Attackers used valid AWS IAM credentials and assumed EC2 roles to make authenticated AWS API requests, and in some cases obtained production secrets despite many blocked attempts.
  • In a separate incident, attackers used a valid AWS identity to read, copy, and delete objects stored in Amazon S3.
  • Arctic Wolf recommends correlating IIS webshell activity with unusual AWS access, reviewing successful API calls during bursts of denials, and revoking or rotating exposed AWS credentials.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam, object-storage, web-server

Products: antifox, artex, alibaba-cloud, amazon-web-services, aws-identity-and-access-management, amazon-s3, amazon-ec2, internet-information-services

Vendors: antifox-ai, alibaba-cloud, amazon, microsoft, arctic-wolf, crowdstrike

A Potential Binance Employee’s Mac Was Infected Seconds After a Fake Homebrew Ad — Should Read

An anonymized infostealer log suggests a potential Binance employee’s Mac was compromised by MacSync just 16 seconds after clicking a Google ad leading to a fake Homebrew page in March 2026. The stolen data included a Mac password, Okta-related credentials, and access to internal data-platform tools, but the report finds no evidence linking this specific infection to Binance’s later theft.

  • On March 24, 2026, a potential Binance employee’s Chrome browser reached macdev.slab.com through a Google ad, based on recorded Google click and analytics cookies.
  • The log indicates that osascript began running 16 seconds after the ad click and collected system information into a /tmp/sync1014991/ folder, artifacts the article says match documented MacSync behavior.
  • The stolen log contained the Mac login password, 532 saved credentials, Okta-related passwords, and credentials for Binance-linked data-platform services including Kibana, Airflow, Kafka, Zeppelin, and Git.
  • The article states that the log does not support identifying the affected person as Binance’s disclosed Wallet DevOps Engineer A and contains no wallet systems, container-deployment token, or internal AI-tool session.
  • The report says there is no evidence that this infostealer log was used in the October 29, 2026 Binance theft.

Technologies: operating-system, browser, identity-provider, iam, package-registry, source-control, message-queue

Products: macos, macbook-air-m3, google-chrome, google-ads, homebrew, okta, macsync, git, apache-kafka

Vendors: apple, google, homebrew, okta, slab, constella-intelligence, huntress

eBPF Rootkits: Why Underground Actors Are Taking Notice — Optional

eBPF’s legitimate kernel capabilities are increasingly being adapted into stealthy Linux rootkits that can hide processes, filter traffic, and activate on crafted network packets without loading traditional kernel modules. Defenders should tightly restrict eBPF privileges, inventory loaded programs and XDP attachments, and monitor for suspicious BPF activity and packet triggers.

  • Flare reported that Russian-language underground forum posts shared eBPF rootkit code and instructions for hiding processes and activating implants with specially crafted network packets.
  • eBPF programs can operate through Linux’s legitimate bpf() interface without loading a traditional kernel module, so routine lsmod checks may not detect them.
  • Prior Linux malware and research projects, including BPFDoor, Symbiote, ebpfkit, TripleCross, Boopkit, and LinkPro, have demonstrated BPF or eBPF techniques for stealth, traffic handling, or remote activation.
  • Flare found that one tutorial described hooking getdents64 to hide processes, using XDP to inspect incoming HTTP traffic, and encrypting command-and-control traffic with AES-256-GCM.
  • The article recommends that Linux operators audit loaded eBPF programs, restrict eBPF privileges, patch BPF verifier flaws, and watch for unexpected XDP programs and suspicious packet triggers.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: linux-kernel

Vendors: flare

item.title: Qlik Sense Attacks, Windows DHCP CVE-2026-88243, and CRAFTY FALCON API Fraud
item.content:encoded:
Window: 11 Nov 11:00 → 11 Nov 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

CERT-In’s CRAFTY FALCON Advisory: AI Is the Accelerant, Your Payment APIs Are the Target — Must Read

CERT-In warns that the active CRAFTY FALCON campaign is using AI-assisted offensive tools to exploit weak staging environments, shared credentials, and trusted payment API paths to steal funds from Indian financial organizations. Defenses should prioritize strict production isolation, short-lived secrets, server-side payment validation, cloud monitoring, and rapid fraud detection.

  • CERT-In says the active CRAFTY FALCON campaign targets Indian NBFCs, digital lenders, fintechs, payment firms, and cryptocurrency exchanges by abusing their payment and disbursement APIs.
  • The campaign gains access through exposed UAT or staging servers, hardcoded API tokens, plaintext credentials, missing MFA, and flaws in file-upload or deserialization functionality.
  • Attackers move from non-production to production environments through shared credentials and network paths, then use legitimate AWS Systems Manager and Lambda channels to run commands.
  • CERT-In reports that attackers test routes with Rs 1 transfers before sending larger amounts to mule accounts, including through merchant settlement APIs.
  • The advisory recommends separating non-production from production, replacing IP-based trust with server-side signed requests and mutual TLS or scoped keys, rotating long-lived secrets, and monitoring cloud-control-plane activity.

Technologies: cloud-platform, remote-access, container-platform, source-control

Products: artex, pentagi, cairn, cyberstrikeai, aws-systems-manager, aws-lambda, github

Vendors: amazon-web-services, docker, github

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-88243) Windows DHCP Server Remote Code Execution via Out-of-Bounds Read — Must Read

Microsoft’s November 2026 updates patch CVE-2026-88243, a critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw in the Windows DHCP Server service affecting Windows Server 2016 through 2025. Organizations should urgently patch DHCP servers and block untrusted inbound UDP/67 exposure.

  • CVE-2026-88243 is a critical out-of-bounds read flaw in the Windows DHCP Server service that can allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute code remotely over a network.
  • Microsoft addressed the vulnerability in its November 2026 security updates, with affected Windows Server 2016, 2019, 2022, and 2025 builds requiring the relevant fixes.
  • The vulnerability has a CVSS v3.1 score of 9.8 and requires no credentials, privileges, user interaction, or high attack complexity.
  • At the time of writing, the issue was not listed in CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and no public proof of concept had been reported.
  • Organizations should inventory servers with the DHCP Server role, block inbound UDP/67 from untrusted networks, audit cloud security groups, and monitor DHCP Server logs for crashes or unexpected restarts.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: windows-server, windows-dhcp-server, cycognito-platform

Vendors: microsoft, cycognito

Hackers Target Qlik Sense Servers With Reverse Shells, Stage ActiveMQ and Veeam Exploits — Should Read

Threat actors targeted Qlik Sense servers in Europe with PowerShell reverse shells and infrastructure containing ActiveMQ and Veeam exploit tooling, echoing tactics associated with past CACTUS ransomware intrusions. Organizations should patch Qlik Sense and monitor for scheduler.exe-launched PowerShell, OpenSSH persistence, and connections to 45.115.26.23.

  • Cynet detected attempts in October 2026 to run PowerShell reverse-shell commands on Qlik Sense servers belonging to several European Union-based customers within a period of just over three minutes.
  • The attempted reverse shell connected to 45.115.26[.]23 on port 4455 and was executed under scheduler.exe, but the attempts were blocked.
  • The exact Qlik Sense vulnerability used in the latest activity is unknown, although the activity overlaps with a November 2023 CACTUS ransomware campaign that exploited Qlik Sense flaws.
  • Analysis of the attackers’ infrastructure found a Windows Go backdoor, SSH persistence scripts, an Apache ActiveMQ exploit for CVE-2023-46604, and a modified Veeam toolchain for CVE-2024-40711.
  • A PowerShell script variant attempted to install OpenSSH and create a scheduled task named WinUpdCheck to run a reverse shell every five minutes.

Technologies: message-queue, backup, remote-access, operating-system

Products: qlik-sense-enterprise-for-windows, apache-activemq, veeam-backup-replication, windows, openssh, manageengine-unified-endpoint-management-and-security, anydesk

Vendors: qlik, apache-software-foundation, veeam, microsoft, openssh, manageengine, anydesk, cynet

Over 35,000 Grok-Built Apps Exposed Online, Some Leaking Confidential Data and Passwords — Should Read

Researchers found that 35,578 of 37,571 publicly discoverable Grok-built apps were accessible without sign-in, exposing internal and personal data from dozens of organizations, including xAI and X. The issue is amplified by insecure default sharing settings, DNS discoverability, and test apps with flawed access controls.

  • Claroc found 35,578 of 37,571 Grok-built apps online were accessible without sign-in, and estimated that about 2% of the open apps contained high- or critical-severity material.
  • The exposed apps included 24 created by X and SpaceXSI staff, with examples such as a confidential sales-hire onboarding plan, a 594-account sales territory map, and a confidential X advertising proposal to a U.S. federal agency.
  • Researchers identified internal data from 30 additional organizations, including a hospital employee directory, an intensive-care patient briefing, a fire department shift board, and a contractor timesheet application containing employee passwords in plain text.
  • Claroc said Grok publishes apps on grok.me subdomains and defaults the sharing setting to “Anyone with the link,” while passive DNS records can reveal those subdomains.
  • In tests on their own Grok apps, the researchers found that one app had no sign-in protection and another allowed an uninvited account to access, edit, and delete customer data because its membership check was implemented incorrectly.

Products: grok, grok-build, chatgpt

Vendors: xai, claroc, openai

eMudhra Revokes 8 More CAs It Previously Declared Unaffected by Key Compromise — Should Read

eMudhra revoked eight additional intermediate certificate authorities after discovering that their RSA private keys were exported into a Python process during a flawed 2025 key-transfer ceremony, despite initially saying they were unaffected. The incident expands the company’s certificate-authority failures and reinforces its planned exit from the publicly trusted TLS business.

  • eMudhra revoked eight additional intermediate certificate authorities after determining that their RSA private keys had been read from hardware security modules into a Python process during an April 30, 2025 key-transfer practice run.
  • The company had previously said the eight RSA issuers were unaffected, but later concluded it could not demonstrate that their key material had been handled in accordance with its own rules.
  • Six of the newly revoked authorities issued website certificates and two issued code-signing certificates; eMudhra listed 195 certificates from them and said all holders had been moved to new certificates.
  • The same script had reduced eight separate ECDSA private keys to a single leading byte, leading to the October compromise and revocation of those authorities.
  • eMudhra says it knows of no misuse, while Microsoft, Chrome, Firefox, and Apple are ending or limiting trust in certificates from its remaining G1 hierarchy on the stated schedules.

Technologies: browser, operating-system

Products: emsign, utimaco-hsm, crypto4a-hsm, windows, edge, macos

Vendors: emudhra, utimaco, crypto4a, mozilla, microsoft, apple

Poland shuts down government services platform ePUAP following cyberattack — Should Read

Poland temporarily took its ePUAP government services platform offline after detecting and stopping a cyberattack, though officials say no compromise or data theft has been confirmed. The outage also affects ePUAP mailboxes and may disrupt the Trusted Profile digital identity service until security checks are complete.

  • Poland temporarily shut down the ePUAP government services platform after detecting and stopping a cyberattack.
  • ePUAP enables citizens and businesses to submit official documents, communicate with government agencies, and complete administrative procedures online.
  • Officials said ePUAP was taken offline as a precaution and have not confirmed that government systems were accessed or that sensitive information was stolen.
  • ePUAP electronic mailboxes remain unavailable, and the disruption may temporarily affect the Trusted Profile digital identity system.
  • The Ministry of Digital Affairs said services will resume after security specialists complete their work, but did not provide a restoration timeline.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam

Products: epuap, trusted-profile

Vendors: central-information-technology-center

Britain, France set out first guidelines for commercial hacking firms — Should Read

Britain, France, and 12 other governments endorsed voluntary guidelines for commercial spyware and hacking firms, calling for customer vetting, safeguards against misuse, and suspension of sales where abuse is likely. The non-binding rules create no penalties and rely on government buyers and export controls for enforcement.

  • Fourteen governments in the Britain- and France-led Pall Mall Process adopted voluntary guidelines for businesses that develop, sell, or finance commercial cyber intrusion capabilities.
  • The guidelines call on companies to vet customers, implement safeguards against misuse, monitor and report abuses, and halt sales and support when serious misuse presents a credible risk.
  • The guidelines are non-binding, impose no penalties for non-compliance, and are expected to rely on governments that buy the tools and license their export for enforcement pressure.
  • The tools covered can silently penetrate phones and have been used for intelligence and organized-crime investigations but have also been implicated in surveillance of journalists, political officials, activists, and businesses.
  • The guidelines were endorsed at the Pall Mall Process’s third conference, attended by representatives from 43 countries, with signatories including the United Kingdom, France, the United States, Germany, Italy, and Japan.

We Built An Agent That Broke All of Our Security Rules. Here's What We Learned. — Optional

Browser-based AI agents often operate inside a user’s authenticated session, making their actions indistinguishable from the user’s and potentially giving them excessive, untraceable access. Until standards support agent identity, verifiable human delegation, and task-scoped permissions, organizations should discover, constrain, audit, and require step-up approval for sensitive agent-driven actions.

  • Token’s Rehearsal browser agent operates within a user’s authenticated session, so the application server cannot inherently distinguish its actions from those of the user.
  • Because Token controls both Rehearsal and its platform, it can lock the interface while the agent acts, record all agent moves, and limit the agent to read-only dashboard access unless the user approves a change.
  • The article says Chrome and Microsoft provide some controls for agentic browsing, while WebMCP can expose website actions to agents and Web Bot Auth can verify which agent made a request.
  • The article argues that current approaches do not combine agent identity, proof of the person an agent represents, and a permission scope narrower than that person’s access.
  • It recommends that security teams inventory agents that use authenticated sessions, trace their users and access, identify agent-based paths around access controls, and require explicit approval or stronger sign-in checks for sensitive actions.

Technologies: browser, iam

Products: rehearsal, token-platform, google-chrome, microsoft-edge

Vendors: token-security, google, microsoft, w3c, ietf

Field Intelligence #5: Scareware at scale. Investment scams built on AI platforms. — Optional

Confiant reports that ad-tech abuse is enabling mobile scareware, crypto-stealing Android malware, and cloaked investment and tech-support scams at scale. The campaigns use trusted cloud and AI app-builder platforms to evade reputation controls and redirect victims toward fraudulent payments or wallet-draining contracts.

  • ZoidWays is a mobile forced-redirect scareware campaign that peaked at roughly 1.5 million blocked impressions in one day and appeared across at least six buying platforms.
  • A fake Microsoft Teams APK delivered through teamsapk[.]cyou is a remote-access trojan that searches for cryptocurrency seed phrases in clipboard data, accessibility-service data, files, and photos using OCR.
  • PseudoCamo uses AI app-builder platforms including lovable[.]app and base44[.]app to host localized age-gate decoys that redirect visitors to investment-scam pages.
  • D-Shortiez shifted some tech-support scam pages from Azure Blob static websites to BunnyCDN and Microsoft Azure Cloud hosts, adding a fake CAPTCHA before the scam landing page.
  • A UK-targeted Claude-branded scam convinces victims to deploy and fund a purported MetaMask trading-bot contract, whose Start transaction forwards the full balance to the scammer.

Technologies: cloud-platform, object-storage, remote-access

Products: microsoft-teams, azure-blob-storage, microsoft-azure, amazon-cloudfront, lovable, base44, bunny-cdn, cloudflare-pages, metamask, claude

Vendors: microsoft, anthropic, lovable, base44, amazon-web-services, bunny-net, cloudflare, consensys

item.title: Actively Exploited Cisco BroadWorks and Outlook Flaws Lead November Security Updates
item.content:encoded:
Window: 11 Nov 07:00 → 11 Nov 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

CISA flags Cisco BroadWorks flaw as actively exploited in attacks — Must Read

CISA has added Cisco BroadWorks XXE flaw CVE-2026-20320 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after active attacks, reportedly including a campaign against a European telecom provider that exposed sensitive keys and credentials. Organizations should urgently apply Cisco’s patches, especially where the BroadWorks OCI-P service is exposed.

  • CISA added CVE-2026-20320, a high-severity Cisco BroadWorks flaw, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog after confirming active exploitation.
  • The flaw is an unauthenticated XML external entity issue in the BroadWorks Open Client Interface XML parser that can allow attackers to read sensitive configuration information using crafted XML messages.
  • Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies must secure affected systems by November 24 under Binding Operational Directive 26-04, while CISA urged all organizations to prioritize remediation.
  • Malbear Labs reported that a Chinese-speaking threat actor used a jailbroken DeepSeek Flash model to exploit the flaw against a European telecommunications provider and 13 organizations using its infrastructure.
  • According to Malbear Labs, the reported campaign obtained system identity and SSL private keys from a BroadWorks XSP host, potentially enabling impersonation in communications between BroadWorks components.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: cisco-broadworks, broadworks-xsp, deepseek-flash

Vendors: cisco, deepseek

Microsoft Patches 1,259 Flaws, Including Exploited Outlook Bug That May Expose NTLMv2 Hashes — Must Read

Microsoft released patches for 1,259 vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-124194, an actively exploited Outlook flaw that can expose NTLMv2 hashes when a user opens a crafted message file. Organizations should prioritize patching Outlook and internet-exposed systems, with U.S. federal agencies required to remediate the flaw by November 24, 2026.

  • Microsoft released patches for 1,259 vulnerabilities across its software portfolio, marking the second consecutive month with more than 1,000 flaws addressed.
  • Microsoft said CVE-2026-124194 is an actively exploited, moderate-severity Outlook flaw that can cause Outlook to connect to an attacker-controlled network location when a user opens a specially crafted message file.
  • The Outlook flaw could expose NTLMv2 authentication information, which could potentially be used to impersonate the affected user.
  • CISA added CVE-2026-124194 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and required U.S. federal agencies to apply the fix by November 24, 2026.
  • The patch release also includes remote code execution fixes affecting Windows Search, LDAP, Windows Schannel, Windows Virtual Filtering Platform, and Windows Xbox Live Networking Service.

Technologies: operating-system, database, cloud-platform

Products: microsoft-outlook, windows, microsoft-office, sql-server, sharepoint-server, azure-openai, claude

Vendors: microsoft, anthropic

Railway Says Stolen Customer AI Keys Led to $740,000 in Estimated Unauthorized Usage Charges — Should Read

Railway says attackers exploited its build infrastructure in October, stole and decrypted customer AI API keys from up to roughly 100,000 workspaces, and generated an estimated $740,000 in unauthorized usage charges. The company has rotated affected credentials, hardened its build system, and says it will cover fraud costs where AI providers do not refund customers.

  • Railway says AI provider keys stored by customers were stolen during an October breach and used for an estimated $740,000 in unauthorized usage charges.
  • The attacker exploited a previously unknown flaw in Railway’s build system, obtained internal credentials, and decrypted customer environment variables containing AI provider keys.
  • Railway estimates that variables in at most 1.85% of workspaces, or about 100,000 workspaces, may have been exposed, although its logs do not show exactly which variables were decrypted.
  • Railway reset linked-account tokens for 1,852 users, notified affected users, and said it found no evidence of logins to customer accounts using the stolen credentials.
  • Railway says it will cover breach-related charges for Anthropic and OpenRouter keys when providers do not issue refunds, while other providers have different claim and refund processes.

Technologies: cloud-platform, secrets-manager, ci-cd, orchestration, iam, source-control, package-registry

Products: railway, aws-bedrock, google-gemini, openai-api, openrouter, github, temporal

Vendors: railway, aws, google, openai, anthropic, openrouter, github, temporal

Citrus Ransomware: VLESS for traffic, Sn00py for encryption, and LLMs lending a hand — Should Read

Citrus Ransomware targets Russian organizations by abusing compromised contractor accounts, escalating privileges, and spreading Sn00py ransomware through malicious Group Policy Objects. The group combines familiar tools with VLESS/Xray tunnels and apparent LLM-generated scripts, making tight control of third-party access and early detection critical.

  • Citrus Ransomware gained initial access through contractor employee credentials stolen to connect to corporate VPNs or internet-facing RDP terminal servers.

Check Point Research links three espionage clusters targeting telecoms, governments, critical infrastructure, and research organizations across Latin America, Asia, and Europe to CopperDragon, a suspected supplier of the Sparrow malware framework to China-nexus actors. The campaigns use distinct access methods and implants—including watering holes, compromised Linux servers, SquadC, SparrowDoor/SparrowShell, CopperDoor, and CopperDNS—to enable credential theft, persistence, lateral movement, and covert command-and-control.

  • Check Point Research identified three operational clusters—SilentDelivery, OceanGate, and DarkWire—linked through shared infrastructure features and malware-code similarities in the Sparrow framework.
  • SilentDelivery used selective compromised-website campaigns in Europe and Asia to display fake Chrome certificate warnings and deliver SquadC or SparrowDoor through fraudulent certificate-repair installers.
  • OceanGate targeted government organizations and critical infrastructure primarily in Asia, initially compromising internet-facing Linux systems before moving into Windows environments for credential theft, lateral movement, and data collection.
  • DarkWire targeted telecommunications providers and government organizations, initially concentrated in Latin America, using CopperDoor and the DNS-tunneling CopperDNS backdoors.
  • Check Point tracks CopperDragon as a possible developer and supplier of the cross-platform Sparrow framework used by several China-nexus threat actors, including FamousSparrow, Earth Estries, TropicTrooper, and UAT-9244.

Russian hackers compromised government email servers to steal NATO, EU correspondence — Should Read

ESET says Russia-linked Turla hackers compromised government Microsoft Exchange servers in Romania and Kazakhstan using a new stealthy toolkit called Cereal to intercept sensitive emails, including NATO and EU correspondence. The group used the victims’ own Exchange infrastructure as a command hub, making the espionage campaign harder to detect and disrupt.

  • ESET attributed a campaign targeting government Microsoft Exchange servers in Romania and Kazakhstan to Turla, a Russian state-linked espionage group associated with the FSB.
  • The attackers used a previously unknown toolkit called Cereal, including a component named CerealBox, to monitor email traffic and capture selected messages.
  • In Romania, the malware was configured to collect emails exchanged with NATO and European Union institutions.
  • The attackers used compromised Exchange servers themselves to issue commands and manage the operation, reducing reliance on external infrastructure.
  • ESET said it could not determine how the attackers initially accessed the government servers or how much information they obtained.

Binance Warns of iOS Sandbox Escape That Could Expose Crypto Wallet Keys, No Fix Confirmed — Should Read

Binance warned that the publicly released worse_query iOS sandbox escape may let malicious sideloaded apps access other apps’ data, potentially exposing crypto wallet seed phrases, private keys, and credentials on iOS 26 and 27. Apple’s latest updates do not confirm a fix, so users should remove untrusted apps and move funds to a new wallet if compromise is suspected.

  • A researcher known as forcequit published worse_query, an iOS sandbox escape that can let an app access data containers belonging to other apps on iPhones running iOS 26 and 27.
  • Binance warned that exposed app data could include cryptocurrency wallet seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials, though no attacks or theft involving worse_query have been reported.
  • The WQ Files file manager uses worse_query to read, edit, delete, and clear other apps’ data without a jailbreak or kernel exploit, and it is installed through sideloading tools such as AltStore and SideStore.
  • Apple’s iOS 27.2.1 and iOS 26.7.3 security notes do not mention worse_query or an iOS sandbox fix.
  • Binance advised users to remove apps from untrusted sources, update iOS and apps, and move funds to a new wallet created on a clean device if they suspect compromise.

Palantir exec nominated to lead CISA; lame-duck Senate vote is uncertain — May Read

President Trump nominated Palantir CIO Michael LoSapio to lead CISA, but a Senate vote during the crowded lame-duck session is uncertain. If not confirmed before adjournment, the nomination must be resubmitted to an incoming Democratic-majority Senate, where Palantir ties may draw greater scrutiny.

  • President Donald Trump nominated Palantir Chief Information Officer Michael LoSapio to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA).
  • CISA has lacked a Senate-confirmed leader since Trump returned to office, with Nick Andersen serving as acting leader since February after previous nominee Sean Plankey withdrew.
  • During the second Trump administration, CISA lost more than 1,000 personnel—about one-third of its workforce—and its budget was reduced by billions of dollars.
  • It is unclear whether the Senate will consider LoSapio's nomination during the crowded lame-duck session; if it does not, Trump would need to renominate him next year.
  • LoSapio could face greater scrutiny in an incoming Democratic-majority Senate because of his role at Palantir, a software and artificial intelligence company with ties to the Trump administration.

Beyond the Alert: The Case for Rich Network Data — Optional

Corelight argues that effective network incident response depends on rich, searchable network evidence—not just alerts—so analysts and AI can trace activity, validate findings, and understand an attack’s full scope. The sponsored article urges buyers to evaluate NDR tools by how deeply their data supports investigation beyond a guided demo.

  • The article argues that preventing every security incident is not possible, so teams need to find and disrupt activity that has entered their networks.
  • An alert may identify a suspicious connection, but detailed network data is needed to trace activity before, after, and across systems and determine an incident’s scope.
  • Rich network data can include transaction details, packet content, extracted files, searchable history, and context that allows analysts to follow connections over time.
  • AI tools can process large amounts of security data and help investigate unfamiliar services, processes, and log formats, but their outputs still need to be checked against evidence.
  • The article recommends evaluating network security products by investigating an alert beyond a guided demonstration to see whether the available data supports unanticipated questions and deeper analysis.

Hackers now exploit critical Barracuda ESG flaws to gain root access — Must Read

Barracuda warns that attackers are actively exploiting two recently patched flaws in its appliances, which can be chained to bypass authorization and execute commands as root. Customers should apply patches immediately and restrict administrative-interface access to trusted networks.

  • Barracuda warned that attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560, two recently patched flaws affecting its Email Security Gateway and other products.
  • CVE-2026-116606 is an authentication weakness in Barracuda Email Security Gateway that can allow modification of an appliance’s global configuration, while CVE-2026-111560 permits unauthenticated operating-system command injection with root privileges.
  • Barracuda said the vulnerabilities can be combined to bypass authorization controls and obtain root access, but exploitation requires access to an affected device’s administrative interface.
  • The company identified exploitation affecting a small number of organizations and urged customers to manually install the relevant patch if it was not automatically applied.
  • Affected products include Barracuda Email Security Gateway, Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF Control Center, Web Application Firewall, and Web Security Gateway.

Google patches eighth Chrome zero-day exploited in attacks this year — Must Read

Google released emergency Chrome updates to fix CVE-2026-125350, a high-severity use-after-free flaw in the browser's XML component that is already being exploited in the wild. Users should update Chrome to version 157.0.8103.50/.51 as soon as possible.

  • Google released emergency Chrome security updates for CVE-2026-125350, a high-severity use-after-free flaw in Chrome's XML component that it says is being exploited in the wild.
  • The flaw can enable memory corruption when Chrome later accesses memory that has already been freed, potentially allowing attackers to manipulate memory layout and execute malicious code.
  • Google did not disclose details about the observed attacks and said vulnerability details may remain restricted until most users have received the fix.
  • The update is rolling out through Chrome's Stable Desktop channel for Windows, macOS version 157.0.8103.50/.51, and Linux version 157.0.8103.50.
  • CVE-2026-125350 is the eighth Chrome zero-day vulnerability Google has patched this year after evidence of active exploitation.

SAP Patches Four CVSS 10.0 Flaws, Including Two Enabling Remote Code Execution — Must Read

SAP released urgent patches for four unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 flaws affecting NetWeaver and Web Dispatcher, including two remote-code-execution bugs, a SAML login bypass, and SAP Gateway server impersonation. Organizations should prioritize patching exposed systems and restrict direct access to ICM and Gateway ports.

  • SAP released fixes for four unauthenticated vulnerabilities rated CVSS 10.0 in its November Security Patch Day bulletin.
  • CVE-2026-76964 in SAP NetWeaver Internet Communication Manager and CVE-2026-89126 in SAP Web Dispatcher can allow remote code execution through crafted network traffic that corrupts memory.
  • CVE-2026-120017 can allow an attacker to sign in as any user, including privileged users, on affected SAML single-sign-on configurations.
  • CVE-2026-89103 can allow an external attacker to impersonate an SAP application server and take unauthorized actions through SAP Gateway.
  • SAP and RedRays recommend prioritizing the patches, updating kernels and Web Dispatchers together, and restricting direct network access to Gateway and Internet Communication Manager ports.

France Blames Iran for Sabotage Attack on Refrigeration Controllers at About 700 Retail Sites — Must Read

France has attributed an October sabotage campaign against internet-exposed refrigeration controllers at roughly 700 retail sites to Iran’s IRGC-linked Shahid Kaveh unit, causing major food losses and about 20 fires. Authorities urge operators to remove affected Danfoss, Dixell, and Copeland systems from public internet access and restore remote access only through secured networks.

  • France attributed an October sabotage campaign targeting refrigeration controllers at about 700 retail and food-sector sites to Shahid Kaveh, a cyber unit linked to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
  • Attackers remotely accessed Danfoss and Dixell controllers, set unlimited high-temperature defrost cycles, and disabled temperature-probe safety alerts, causing food losses and about 20 fires.
  • Most affected organizations were large French retailers including Casino, Leclerc, Coopérative U, Metro, Carrefour, and Intermarché, while smaller butcher shops, a slaughterhouse, and cooperative food plants were also hit.
  • French authorities opened a judicial investigation, plan to summon Iran’s ambassador, and will seek additional European sanctions against those involved.
  • CERT-FR advised operators to remove affected controllers from public internet access, review configurations, update supported devices, change default passwords, and use a secure VPN or protected network for remote access.

Turla hackers use new Cereal malware to spy on govt Exchange servers — Should Read

Russia-linked Turla used its new Cereal malware framework to covertly spy on Microsoft Exchange email servers at government organizations in Kazakhstan and Romania. The toolset intercepts selected emails and executes commands in memory while avoiding separate command-and-control infrastructure.

  • ESET found Turla's Cereal toolset on Microsoft Exchange servers at a government organization in Kazakhstan in late 2025 and at a Romanian government agency compromised on December 23, 2025.
  • Turla used the CerealBox component to enter Exchange's EdgeTransport.exe process and take over existing email-processing handlers without registering a new handler or interrupting mail delivery.
  • The malware selectively collected emails matching specified sender, recipient, and subject criteria, particularly messages with DOC, DOCX, or PDF attachments.
  • CerealNeuron accepted encrypted requests disguised as legitimate Exchange service paths, ran attacker-provided programs in memory, and returned encrypted results.
  • ESET observed no external command-and-control infrastructure in the campaign, with the compromised Exchange server acting as the attackers' only control point.

Products: microsoft-exchange-server

Apple Patches iMessage Group Chat Privacy Flaws and Bluetooth Pairing Vulnerabilities — Should Read

Apple released security updates fixing iMessage flaws that could expose group-chat messages or allow unauthorized joining, along with an actively exploited Brotli memory-corruption bug and Bluetooth pairing vulnerabilities. Users should install the available updates promptly.

  • Apple released updates that fix iMessage issues that could allow a remote attacker to join a group chat and receive its messages, or allow a newly added member to access messages sent before joining.
  • The iMessage issues are tracked as CVE-2026-113961, an authorization issue addressed through improved validation, and CVE-2026-113960.
  • The same updates fix CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in Google’s Brotli decoder that could allow malicious input to corrupt memory and was added to CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 27.
  • Apple’s iOS 18.7.12 and watchOS 26.6.1 notes list other security fixes but do not list the iMessage or Brotli fixes.
  • All nine updates address Bluetooth and AirPlay issues, including flaws that could allow a malicious nearby Bluetooth device to pair without user interaction or bypass pairing-code attempt limits.

Fireworks AI discloses new breach after cloud provider hack — Should Read

Fireworks AI disclosed a second October breach in which attackers leveraged a compromised third-party cloud provider to access development machines and obtain customer metadata, billing information, and some incomplete model weights and datasets. The company says it contained the incident, rotated credentials, and found no further unauthorized access after October 25.

  • Fireworks AI disclosed that attackers accessed its development machines on October 24 after a third-party cloud provider hosting its research-and-development machines suffered a security incident on October 23.
  • The unauthorized workload run on Fireworks development machines exposed customer resource metadata, billing information, and incomplete model weights and datasets for some customers.
  • Fireworks said payment-card numbers were not exposed because the company does not store them.
  • Fireworks detected the activity on October 24 and said it had found no further evidence of successful unauthorized access to its customer platform as of October 25.
  • The company revoked and replaced credentials and service accounts, restricted unauthorized network paths, isolated affected systems, and is working with Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 on the investigation and security improvements.

Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, claiming stronger coding and cybersecurity capabilities, with Fable 5.2 achieving a 76.3% success rate on Irregular’s multi-stage CyScenarioBench—above GPT-6 Cyber’s 61%.   • Anthropic said Fable 5.2 scored 89.6% on its CVE Rediscovery benchmark, which tests whether a model can rediscover known software flaws using affected source code.
  • Anthropic described Claude Mythos 5.2 as its most capable model for cybersecurity engineering and said its cyber capabilities are available through the Cyber Verification Program.
  • Anthropic updated Claude Security with continuous code scanning and automatic fix tracking to help teams identify and address weaknesses as code changes.

IT threat evolution in Q3 2026. Non-mobile statistics — Optional

Kaspersky’s Q3 2026 telemetry recorded more than 311 million web-based attacks, 23.7 million malicious or unwanted local objects, and ransomware targeting 81,556 users, with Qilin the most prolific extortion group by leak-site victims. The report also highlights active exploitation of enterprise product flaws, growing macOS supply-chain and stealer activity, and shifting IoT botnet attack patterns.

  • In Q3 2026, Kaspersky products blocked 311,083,655 attacks from online resources and Web Anti-Virus detected 46,936,926 unique URLs.
  • Kaspersky protected 81,556 unique users from ransomware attacks in Q3 2026 and detected 4,470 new ransomware variants across three new ransomware families.
  • Qilin accounted for 15.39% of victims published on ransomware groups’ data leak sites during the reporting period, making it the most prolific group in the review.
  • Kaspersky detected miner attacks affecting 217,024 unique users worldwide and identified 2,197 new miner variants in Q3 2026.
  • Kaspersky File Anti-Virus recorded 23,733,652 malicious and potentially unwanted objects, while 10.88% of users’ computers worldwide encountered a local malware threat at least once during the quarter.

IT threat evolution in Q3 2026. Mobile statistics — Optional

Kaspersky recorded 1.67 million blocked mobile threats in Q3 2026, with banking Trojans—especially Mamont—and packaged droppers driving much of the malicious-app activity. The quarter also saw AI-enabled Android fraud tools and iOS spyware campaigns exploiting DarkSword through compromised packages and fake App Store apps.

  • Kaspersky blocked more than 1.66 million attacks involving mobile malware, adware, or unwanted software in Q3 2026, down from 1,996,823 in Q2.
  • Trojan-Banker threats accounted for 31.63% of detected malicious mobile apps, and Kaspersky detected 119,688 mobile banking Trojan installation packages.
  • Kaspersky identified Android apps that used on-device AI models to interpret fraud commands or search screenshots and gallery images for banking information, including CVV codes.
  • The Mamont banking Trojan remained the most active banking threat in attacks, while Creduz accounted for the largest share of detected banking-Trojan packages.
  • iOS campaigns used the DarkSword exploit chain through infected Packagist packages and a fake App Store crypto wallet tracker, with spyware designed to steal data including keychain contents, Wi-Fi passwords, SMS messages, photos, and crypto wallet recovery phrases.
